subject: Sequential PO acknowledgement, ledger mapping, and netterm wedge
messages:
From: Michelle Barnes <mbarnes@northfieldhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@northfieldhealth.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: PO requirements & invoice cadence — Northfield / Redwood

Hi Vivek / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has one set of constraints we need to lock before Legal will issue the PO. High-level asks below — can you confirm whether the discount tiers we discussed are contingent on any of these fields being present on the PO?

- PO metadata: we must have a single top-level PO number per legal entity (no line-item-only POs).
- GL/BU mapping: separate remit codes for three business units — system requires the PO to include BU tags.
- Invoice cadence: our AP team prefers weekly invoices but will accept monthly consolidated statements if there's a stated schedule.
- Net terms: Finance is pushing for net60. We know Redwood usually offers net45 for enterprise; is there an ingress path to get the 10% tier with net60?
- Early-pay: if we move to monthly statements, would an early-pay incentive be available (e.g., 2% within 15 days)?

I've attached our standard PO template (Northfield_PO_template.pdf). If you can confirm the discount trigger logic and whether Redwood can accept a staggered invoice flow (one consolidated monthly invoice with PO header referencing multiple BU tags), we can route to Legal.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement needs this clarified before EOD next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Michelle
Michelle Barnes
Sr. Procurement Manager | Northfield Health
attachments: Northfield_PO_template.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Michelle Barnes <mbarnes@northfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO requirements & invoice cadence — Northfield / Redwood

Hi Michelle — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and a proposed path forward below. I’m looping Ben (sales ops) and Vanessa (enterprise sales lead) to confirm the commercial plumbing.

Short answers:
- Discount eligibility is tied to PO header presence + required fields. Specifically we require: PO number, remit entity (legal entity name), and at least one BU/GL tag in the header (not just on line items). If the PO includes those three, it will be eligible for tiered discounts.
- Staggered invoice flow: we can accept a consolidated monthly statement that references multiple internal BU tags, provided each invoice line maps back to a PO header and we receive an initial acceptance acknowledgement for each BU (our AR system needs the header-to-line mapping).
- Net terms: our standard enterprise path for the 10% tier is net45 with signed commitment. Net60 is atypical — we can make a one-time concession for net60 but that would reduce the discount by ~2 percentage points unless there's an advance-commitment or payment guarantee.
- Early-pay incentive: we can offer 2% if payments are posted within 15 days on monthly statements, with early-pay tracked on the invoice/ERPs. That incentive can be layered with a smaller base discount if Northfield takes net60.

Proposed next steps:
1) If you can return a sample PO filled with the header fields (PO number, remit entity, BU tags) we will run it through our AR ingest to validate mapping.
2) Ben to provide a redline of the Order Form showing net45 (standard) vs net60-with-reduced-discount so your FP&A can compare economics.
3) If Northfield wants to insist on strict net60 with full 10% discount, we will need either an escrow/guarantee or a staggered prepay (e.g., 25% upfront) — we can outline that option in the order form.

Attaching Redwood_PRICING_BREAKDOWN.xlsx so you can see the adjusted discount scenarios (Ben, please confirm the numbers).

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_PRICING_BREAKDOWN.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Michelle Barnes <mbarnes@northfieldhealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO requirements & invoice cadence — Northfield / Redwood

Michelle — following up with the finance mechanics Vivek mentioned. A few clarifications from my side: 

- PO header gating: our billing system flags any invoice that arrives without the header fields and routes it to manual processing. Manual-processing invoices do not qualify for tier discounts and can add 7–10 business days to recognition. So to preserve the commercial terms, we need the header present on day-one.
- Netterm wedge: the delta between net45 @10% and net60 @8% in your expected spend translates to ~1.4% annual cash impact — I’ve inserted example numbers in the attached pricing sheet.
- Consolidated monthly statements: we can accept them, but we require an acceptance ACK per BU (simple one-line confirmation is fine). The acceptance ACKs can be emailed to invoices@redwood.com and referenced on the consolidated invoice. That avoids line-item level discrepancies during ERPs.
- EDI/ERP ingestion: if Northfield can export a CSV of PO headers post-issue, we can ingest into our system the same day (requires SFTP or secure POST). If not, we can onboard via manual intake for the first month and then switch to EDI.

Options to-hit-10% tier (summary):
A) Net45, PO header present, BU tags in header = eligible for full 10%
B) Net60 without escrow = eligible for 8% (automatic)
C) Net60 + 25% prepay OR a short-term payment guarantee = eligible for 10%
D) Net60 + early-pay 2% for payment within 15 days on monthly statement = effectively reduces cost but technically counts as separate incentive (finance prefers A or C).

If you’re open to scenario C, we can put the prepay milestone into the order form with a simple proof of funds clause. Otherwise, Ben will prepare a clean order form showing A and B side-by-side for your CFO.

Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_PRICING_BREAKDOWN.xlsx

From: Michelle Barnes <mbarnes@northfieldhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO requirements & invoice cadence — Northfield / Redwood

Thanks all — appreciate the detail. Quick response from Procurement / FP&A after reviewing the scenarios:

- We can move to Net45 for year one to secure the 10% tier if Redwood will commit to a quarterly review of usage and an explicit cap on any rate-card increases. That lets our CFO get comfortable with the cash profile and gives Redwood the standard commercial.
- If Redwood prefers to keep net60, we will consider option C (25% prepay) but it needs to be on the order form as a refundable credit against the first two invoices.
- For onboarding speed, we will provide a sample filled PO (using your header fields) by Monday lunchtime. We will also populate the BU tag in the header.

Please prepare an order form with two variants (Net45 @10% with quarterly review clause; Net60 @8% with 25% refundable prepay). We’ll circulate to Legal after we receive it. Also confirm the email address for acceptance ACKs (invoices@redwood.com) so AP can route correctly.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Michelle
Michelle Barnes
Sr. Procurement Manager | Northfield Health
attachments: none
